subject: mathematics
question_text: Show that the line joining the pair of points 6a−4b+4c and −4c, and the line joining the pair of points −a−2b−3c and a+2b−5c, intersect at the point −4c, where a, b, c are non-coplanar vectors.

mark_split.label: Write the vector equation of the first line
Write the vector equation of the second line
Substitute back to reach the given point

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.61 — SAQ chapter 8 Addition of Vectors, answer 55. Printed appearances: AP 22 · TS 22. Unlike answer 54 this one NAMES the meeting point, so the work has to land on −4c rather than discover it — which is why the useful parameter turns out to be t = 0. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — no [N Marks] tags are printed anywhere in this chapter. It follows the split the same book prints for the one 4-mark answer that does carry tags, Matrices answer 40 on book p.51. The book's chapter header carries ★★★ and reads '4 Marks'; that star is the CHAPTER's rank, not this question's. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B runs Q11-Q17 at 4 marks each, answer any 5 of 7; Q12 is the Addition of Vectors slot. NOTE: Addition of Vectors has NO Section-C slot on the paper and no LAQ chapter in this book — the unit is SAQ and VSAQ only.

steps.why: Choosing WHICH two equations to combine is the skill. The a and c ones were built to have +2s and −2s, so adding them is the one step that removes s in a single line.
common_mistakes: Substituting one equation into another and grinding through fractions.
